findings.evidence: Lines 49-53 (Terminology Notes section): Mix of 'You record the stipend item on the request form', 'Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log', 'Payroll releases the covered purchase amount', 'Countersign the employee request within two business days.' Also line 45 mixing second-person and corporate voice: 'You must keep your equipment...and we may ask...'
findings.fix: Clearly separate sections and instructions by audience. Create distinct subsections for employee responsibilities, manager responsibilities, and finance/payroll responsibilities, or add explicit labels (e.g., 'For Managers:' or 'For Finance Staff:') to clarify which audience each instruction targets.
findings.location: Terminology Notes section (lines 49-53) and How to Apply section (line 45)
findings.violation: The document addresses multiple distinct audiences (employees, managers, finance staff, payroll staff) within the same sections without clear separation. The 'Terminology Notes' section mixes employee instructions ('You record', 'you submit', 'You track') with manager/finance/payroll instructions ('Countersign the employee request', 'Finance reconciles', 'Payroll releases') in a way that makes it unclear which instructions apply to which reader.

findings.evidence: Lines 5, 27, 61, 73 use different names for what may be the same list: 'equipment catalog' (5, 61), 'approved list' (27), 'vendor list' (73). findings.fix: Choose one consistent term for each concept and use it throughout. Add a defined-terms section at the beginning or create a table explaining relationships (e.g., 'equipment catalog = approved list = vendor list'). Clarify whether 'proof of purchase' and 'receipt' mean the same thing.
findings.location: Throughout document, particularly Program Overview (line 5), Approval Timeline (line 27), Special Cases (line 61), Questions and Updates (line 73); Required Documentation section (lines 33-35)
findings.violation: Central terms for the same or related concepts vary inconsistently throughout the document without explanation of whether they are the same thing or different. 'Equipment catalog', 'approved list', and 'vendor list' appear to be the same document but use different names; 'reimbursement log' and 'request log' may be the same; 'proof of purchase' and 'receipt' are used interchangeably without clarification.

findings.evidence: Line 11: 'The stipend covers one claim' (stipend is abstract; should be 'You receive one claim'). findings.fix: Rewrite sentences to name the actual actor. Replace 'The stipend covers' with 'You receive', 'eligibility applies' with 'You are eligible', 'the portal walks through' with 'you walk through', and 'the request moves' with '[Role] processes the request'.
findings.location: Throughout document: Program Overview (implied), Eligibility section (lines 11, 15), How to Apply section (lines 19, 21), Approval Timeline (line 29), Reimbursement Amounts (line 39), Restrictions section (line 47), Terminology Notes (line 51)

findings.evidence: Terminology Notes (lines 49-53): Covers employee, finance, payroll, and manager actions in six sentences with no clear theme connecting them. Program Coordination (lines 63-65): 'The benefits team coordinates every stipend request from intake to payout' (sentence 1) followed by 'A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses' (sentence 2), 'Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year' (sentence 3), and 'The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter' (sentence 4).
findings.fix: For Terminology Notes: Either expand into separate subsections for each role, or clarify the section's purpose with a clearer heading and opening sentence that explains how these definitions connect. For Program Coordination: Delete the unrelated sentences about audit, guidance, and budget, or move them to appropriate sections elsewhere. Rewrite to focus on a single theme: how the benefits team manages the stipend request lifecycle.
findings.location: Terminology Notes section (lines 49-53) and Program Coordination section (lines 63-65)
findings.violation: Two sections lack coherent themes that a reader can identify. The 'Program Coordination' section opens with stipend coordination but then lists three completely unrelated topics (audit of travel expenses, federal guidance on remote work, coffee budget reset), so a reader cannot identify what the section is actually about.
